---
title: "Add a method"
guide-section: How-to
---

This adds a renderer drawn with PyVista and offers it as `patch.scene.tube()`. Any backend and namespace work the same way.

## Write the renderer

In `src/dasviz/pv/tube.py`, import the backend inside the function, and declare it with `requires`:

```python
from dasviz import requires
from dasviz.prep import color_limits


@requires("pyvista")
def tube(patch, *, scale=None, scale_type="relative"):
    """Draw the fiber as a tube colored by the data."""
    import pyvista as pv

    limits = color_limits(patch.data, scale, scale_type)
    ...
```

Never import PyVista at the top of the module: dasviz's namespaces are loaded whether or not it is installed. A type used only in annotations goes under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`.

Work out anything that isn't drawing (limits, decimation, geometry) in `dasviz.prep`, where it can be tested without PyVista.

## Bind it to a namespace

Export it from `src/dasviz/pv/__init__.py`, then in `src/dasviz/namespaces/scene.py`:

```python
from dasviz.pv import tube


class ScenePatch(DasvizPatchNamespace):
    name = "scene"
    tube = tube
```

## Test and document it

- Put tests in `tests/pv/`, starting with `pv = pytest.importorskip("pyvista")`. `PYVISTA_OFF_SCREEN` is set for the whole suite.
- Add it to the reference in `great-docs.yml`.
- Run `uv run pytest`. The existing tests check that the method declares its backend and that loading dasviz still imports none.

## A new backend

Add an entry to `BACKENDS` in `src/dasviz/_deps.py`, and in `pyproject.toml` an extra, its alias, and its place in `all`. The tests check these agree.
